q1.desc: Pollinators keep the world fed. Find and ID three of them today — bees, butterflies, hoverflies, beetles, anything that visits a flower for a snack.
q1.tip1: Honeybees count, hoverflies count, even beetles on flowers count.
q1.tip2: Morning sun + a flowering patch is the cheat code.

q2.desc: Beetles. Crunchy. Misunderstood. Bag yourself any species in order Coleoptera.
q2.tip1: Flip a log (gently) — most beetles love the dark.
q2.tip2: Try the underside of leaves at dusk.

q3.desc: A real trophy. Track down a Legendary-tier insect this week. Luna Moth, Atlas Moth, or anything wearing five stars.
q3.tip1: Legendaries cluster at dusk near porch lights.
q3.tip2: Check the Map for recent rare sightings nearby.

q4.desc: ID at least one bug a day for seven days in a row. Doesn't matter what — a single ant counts.
q4.tip1: Missed a day? Toughens you up. Start the count again.
q4.tip2: Set a reminder when your streak hits 5 — the home stretch is brutal.

confirm.networkBody: Critterboard works fully offline. Turning Network on lets it send your display name, your caught species with times, and (only if you switch it on) exact catch locations to our server, for rankings and friends. You can delete all of it again at any time.
confirm.boardBody: Your display name and XP become visible to every player in the global and weekly rankings. You can hide yourself again at any time.
confirm.locBody: Each new catch is uploaded with its exact location and appears, without your name, on the maps of players nearby who show sightings. You can switch this off to remove the stored locations.

confirm.crashBody: When the app crashes, it sends the error, your phone model, system version and app version to Sentry, our crash service. No name, photos, catches or location.

help.webLabel: Open the full help page on critterboard.app
help.title: Help & About

faq1.a: Yes. Vision, chat, and the species database all run on your phone. The only reason to turn on Network access is to share to the leaderboard or post sightings publicly.

faq2.q: Why is my ID confidence low?
faq2.a: Usually one of three things: the photo is blurry, the bug fills less than 1/4 of the frame, or you're outside an installed regional pack. Scans under your match threshold (Brains, 33% by default) can't be added at all. Try a closer crop, brighter light, and a side profile.

faq3.a: You earn one freeze every 7 days of activity, capped at three banked. If you miss a day, the freeze auto-spends to keep your streak alive. You don't have to do anything.

faq4.q: Can I use Critterboard if I'm colorblind?
faq4.a: Yes. All confidence and rarity cues double-encode with shape and label. There's a high-contrast pass in development; ping us if a specific screen is hurting you.

faq5.q: Where do reference images come from?
faq5.a: iNaturalist (CC-BY-NC) for photos; GBIF for ranges. We don't train on your photos — model updates ship from our side only.

faq6.q: How do I delete my data?
faq6.a: Everything on this phone: scroll down to "Wipe everything". It removes your dex, sightings, settings and on-device models, and deletes your online data first. Online only: Brains has "Delete my online data". There is no undo.

faq7.q: Can I move my data to a new phone?
faq7.a: Yes. Use "Back up my data (file)" here, keep the file in Files or iCloud Drive, then "Restore from a backup" on the new phone (or on the first screen after a reinstall). It adds your dex, catches, quests and settings; photos and chat history aren't included.

faq8.q: Where do habitat, size, range and diet come from?
faq8.a: Habitat and diet are typical for the species' family. Size comes from Wikipedia and range from GBIF records, so a few species show the family instead of a size. "Read more on Wikipedia" opens the full article.
